To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the azimuthal anisotropy of the midrapidity protons in the collision of heavy ions increases with the transverse momentum and decreases with the beam energy.
the azimuthal anisotropy increases with transverse momentum, decreases with increasing energy and is much larger for composite than for proton emission.
the out-of-plane to in-plane ratio of the emission of protons is strongly dependent on the transverse momentum, and decreases with increasing incident energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the out-of plane emission of light fragments and protons at midrapidity in symmetric heavy-ion reactions at bombarding energies of E/A=400,700 and 100 MeV.
the study of the out-of plane emission of protons, deuterons and alpha particles at 400 MeViA in the reactions 209Bi+209Bial.
the question whether the azimuthal anisotropy of the out-of plane emission of protons can be explained by the emission of protons from excited fragments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the out-of-plane enhanced emission is due to the reaction plane anisotropy of the initial density profile.
the anisotropy is caused by anisotropic emission of nucleons and light fragments in the initial reaction stage, which is not influenced by the subsequent evolution of the system.

the emission pattern of the light particles in heavy-ion collisions is determined by the initial reaction plane and that the anisotropic flow is caused by the initial momentum anisotropy of the reaction plane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the anisotropy is caused by an anisotropy of the source and not by a preferential emission direction in the reaction plane.
the out-of-plane enhancement of mid-rapidity protons and light fragment is stronger at 400 MeVs/A than at higher energies.
the out-of-plane anisotropy increases with increasing mass and transverse momentum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the azimuthal emission of protons is not only determined by the collective flow of the reaction but also by the reaction plane itself.
we observe a strong azimuthal anisotropy for midrapidity particles at all bombarding energy and that the effect is stronger for composite particles than for protons.
we have found evidence of an enhanced production of particles in a plane perpendicular to the reaction-plane.
